messages:
maria_g: Hey team - getting an escalated ticket from FluxAI. They see a sustained ~20m burst of 502/504s hitting Hosted API (us-east-1). Customer says streaming responses cut mid-token and client sees HTTP/2 RST_STREAM. Sample trace ids: trace=abc123ef, trace=def456gh.

ashley_su: Thanks Maria — can you paste a short repro or a sample request + headers? any recent deploys or auth rotations around the time?

maria_g: Copying sample curl they sent (sanitized):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "x-tenant: fluxai" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}' --http2
```
We rolled a small config deploy at 2024-11-07T12:57:00Z but spike started ~12:58-13:20Z. JWT rotation also shows at 12:59Z for the auth tier.

ops-bot: [ALERT] envoy.upstream.reset_rate (us-east-1) increased 420% over baseline at 2024-11-07T12:59:30Z. Related runbook: https://internal/runbooks/upstream-reset

devin_ops: Can we grep envoy logs for those trace ids and check upstream connection pool saturation/keepalive timeouts? Also check if auth proxy returned 503s which could cascade. Quick commands: `sudo journalctl -u envoy --since "2024-11-07 12:55" | grep abc123ef` and `kubectl exec -n infra envoy-xxx -- curl -s localhost:9901/stats | grep upstream_cx_`

lia_reliability: I pulled a snippet from envoy logs around trace=abc123ef: 
```
[2024-11-07T12:59:31.102Z] envoy info: cluster upstream_auth remote=10.10.5.23:443 -> upstream reset: connection reset by peer
[2024-11-07T12:59:31.103Z] stream concluded: grpc status 14, response 502
[2024-11-07T12:59:31.104Z] connpool: h2 stream window exhausted, dropping stream
```
That matches an auth backend flapping and Envoy closing streams. Not seeing immediate OOM or CPU spikes on the proxy pods.

ashley_su: Do we have auth tier traces? if auth backend is returning intermittent 503/502 it will cause envoys to surface 502/504. Maria, can you confirm FluxAI requests were hitting the same tenant header (x-tenant) every time, and whether client was using connection reuse?

maria_g: Customer confirmed they use long-lived connections and connection reuse. They also noted the problem disappeared when they retried with new TCP connection. I pulled auth rotation log — rotation job started at 12:59:00Z and did a quick key publish: `auth-rotation: published new jwk set to s3://authkeys/rot-2024-11-07.json`

devin_ops: Hypothesis: JWT rotation caused a brief surge in auth backend (cache misses), combined with h2 keepalive window exhaustion on Envoy for long-lived streams, leading to RST/502s for streaming customers. Mitigation options: 1) temporarily scale auth replicas + increase upstream connection pool and h2 max concurrent streams on frontdoor; 2) enable short-lived retry/fallback for streaming endpoints so ephemeral auth errors return 5xx->retry internally (not expose 502 to clients). Can we try (1) first?

lia_reliability: I'll patch a canary config to bump `upstream.request_max_concurrent_streams` and `connection_pool_size` in us-east frontdoor and scale auth to +2 replicas. Rolling that now to a small subset (10% shards).

maria_g: Sending tcpdump sample and the customer's minimal repro. Also will loop in CS to tell FluxAI we're investigating. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ashley_su: Awesome — please attach the tcpdump and the envoy admin stats output when you have them and paste the final rollback/tweak notes here so I can close the ticket with remediation steps.

lia_reliability: Patch live on canary; monitoring shows reset_rate trending down after scale + pool bump. Will watch for 15m and then promote if stable.

maria_g: Noted. collecting artifacts now and will update ticket with timeline and runbook links.
